stories.title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
stories.description: Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing. A hybrid compute-and-store core combining thermally coupled vanadium dioxide leaky integrate-and-fire neurons with domain-wall racetrack memory is presented. This architecture preserves temporal spike histories and achieves high recognition accuracy with low power consumption.

stories.title: Copper derived from deep-sea hydrothermal vent minerals facilitates hydrogen cyanide formation from glycine in alkaline aqueous environment
stories.description: In prevailing origin of life scenarios, hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is a key molecule for forming life’s essential building blocks, as demonstrated by HCN-centric prebiotic chemistry. However, whether HCN can be in-situ generated near deep-sea hydrothermal vents (HVs) has remained unexplored. Here, we show that a Cu-rich natural HV mineral reacts with glycine to generate HCN under alkaline, anaerobic conditions. Using 13C-isotopic labelled glycine, in-situ generation of HCN from glycine is confirmed, reaching concentration of 451.42 nM at 25 °C in 24 hours. HCN yield increases threefold at 10 °C. Copper leaching, and HCN generation from a glycine-CuCl2 mixture, or from synthetic Cu(Gly)2 in an anaerobic alkaline solution, indicate that copper(II) functions as an oxidant in this process. Because glycine can be generated through multiple pathways, our findings integrate cyanide chemistry into alkaline Cu-bearing HV environments, expanding the chemical diversity accessible within alkaline vent environments and potentially analogous systems beyond Earth.

stories.title: Genome-resolved microbial communities across stratified freshwater lakes in Japan
stories.description: Stratified freshwater lakes have vertically structured microbial communities with key roles in biogeochemical cycles. Despite the increasing availability of sequencing data, the number of standardized depth-paired datasets across lakes with different mixing regimes and trophic levels remain limited. Japan offers the opportunity to study lakes with diverse geological histories, trophic levels and mixing regimes within a relatively confined geographical region. Here we present a comparative metagenomic resource, which includes the four deep systems Lake Biwa, Lake Inawashiro, Lake Toya, and Lake Chuzenji. Eight metagenomic samples were collected in September 2022 from epilimnion and hypolimnion and were sequenced using both Illumina short-read and Nanopore long-read technologies. We recovered 569 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 204 high-quality genomes, 58 circular genomes, with 36.7% of all MAGs representing putative novel species. In addition to genomic data, this dataset includes physicochemical variables for the analyzed samples (e.g. oxygen saturation, temperature, pH, conductivity) as well as nutrient and organic carbon concentrations.

stories.title: Sources and drivers of antibiotic resistance genes across rivers and lakes
stories.description: River and lake ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet the global distribution, sources and risks of their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here we analysed 4,128 river and lake metagenomes (water and sediment) from 42 countries and regions and constructed a comprehensive genome-resolved catalogue of ARG-carrying bacteria, revealing key pathogenic vectors of resistance. Clinically important ARGs, including blaOXA and mcr, were widespread and showed distinct biogeographical patterns, highlighting rivers and lakes as potential sentinels for global antimicrobial resistance surveillance. Here, using an integrative source-tracking framework, we identified aquaculture, hospital sewage and municipal sewage as major contributors to riverine resistomes, with the estimated contribution of aquaculture increasing from 11% in 2012 to 40% in 2020. Human population and aquaculture intensity emerged as key drivers of the distribution and associated risks of river and lake resistomes. We further generated a predictive global map of freshwater resistome risk. By transforming metagenomic data into a tool for tracing antimicrobial resistance, our study establishes rivers as potential early-warning systems and supports their integration into One Health surveillance frameworks. A comprehensive analysis of river and lake resistomes reveals the growing contribution of aquaculture to antimicrobial resistance in rivers and offers insights to strengthen environmental surveillance and early-warning systems.

stories.title: Ebola virus-based antibody products cross-neutralize 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein
stories.description: The ongoing 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease has highlighted the urgent need for therapeutic countermeasures. Whether Ebola virus (EBOV)-induced antibodies can cross-neutralize contemporary BDBVs is unclear. Here we test a diverse panel of EBOV-derived polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies, including plasma from humans after EBOV infection and horse plasma and mice serum immunized with available EBOV immunogens, against vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudotypes presenting BDBV-2026 glycoprotein (GP). We find that all antibodies retain cross-neutralizing activity against BDBV-2026 glycoprotein. These findings identify existing Ebola virus-derived antibody preparations as candidates for rapid evaluation. Antibodies raised by Ebola virus retain neutralizing activity against the glycoprotein of the Bundibugyo virus causing the 2026 outbreak, supporting the rapid evaluation of existing Ebola antibody products in the current outbreak.

stories.title: Multidimensional motor unit control after paralysing spinal cord injury using non-invasive recordings
stories.description: Spinal cord injury results in profound motor impairment, which affects approximately 20 million people worldwide. Regaining hand use is one of their highest priorities. Interestingly, even severely affected individuals can still use spared connections to generate detectable activity (measured with electromyography) in their paralysed muscles when attempting to perform a movement. Here we asked whether participants with no hand function due to a cervical spinal cord injury could still control the activity of motor units from paralysed muscles, which we detected using high-density surface electromyographic recordings. Participants could readily control their motor units to accurately perform three different one-dimensional tracking tasks that imposed different control requirements, with performance plateauing after a few days of practice. Moreover, this accurate control readily transferred to a two-dimensional cursor navigation task, allowing participants to play a series of one-dimensional (‘Pong’) and two-dimensional (‘Snake’) games and to navigate a virtual wheelchair using three independent control signals. This robust performance was achieved despite the presence of spasticity, and even in one participant who had a motor complete injury. These findings demonstrate the promise of non-invasive motor unit recordings for restoring hand function and suggest potential avenues for rehabilitation after paralysis. Yang, Rawji, Gibbs and colleagues show that participants with spinal cord injury can modulate the activity of motor units from their paralysed hand to control a computer cursor in 3D, play video games and drive a virtual wheelchair.

stories.title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
stories.description: The photon avalanche effect exhibits a large optical nonlinear response, which is crucial for advancement in super-resolution imaging and optical sensing. However, photon avalanche systems with nonlinearity exceeding 100 remain confined to a single band in the near-infrared region, where standard detectors have low sensitivity. Here, we show that a cascade amplified photon avalanche strategy via lattice reconstruction to address these limitations. Introducing lutetium substitution into the host lattice enhances interionic energy exchange and cross-relaxation, activating multiple visible emission channels of holmium and erbium ions with amplified nonlinearities. A nonlinearity order of up to 560 is achieved in ~216 nm nanoparticles, while 43 nm nanoparticles retain a nonlinearity of 183 and enable super-resolution microscopy with 28 nm lateral resolution. We further demonstrate multi-color super-resolution microscopy and sub-cellular bioimaging. Benefiting from high detection efficiency and flexible wavelength selection, cascade amplified photon avalanche nanoprobes are promising for ultrasensitive sensing and super-resolution lithography beyond optical imaging. This work extends and amplifies the nonlinear response of Tm³⁺ photon avalanche into the highly detectable visible region with optical nonlinearities exceeding 550, enabling sound 28-nm spatial resolution and multi-channel bioimaging application.
